# Slice Product Change

## Purpose

Decompose one approved Product Change into Delivery Slices: coherent, implementable, verifiable
product increments, each preserving a vertical product outcome through the stack. Each slice later
becomes one backlog item and one handoff. This skill proposes the decomposition and its rationale;
a human approves every slice.

## When to use

- A Product Change has status `approved` and has no slices yet, or its slicing needs revision.
- The human asks for a slicing proposal, or for existing draft slices to be reworked.

Do not use this skill on a change that is still `draft` or `proposed` — slicing an unapproved
change front-runs approval point 1. Do not use it to generate handoffs (use `prepare-sdd-handoff`).

## Required inputs

- The Product Change ID (`CHG-...`) with status `approved`.
- Access to the change directory `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/` and the baseline
  `docs/product/model`.
- A working `product-definition` CLI.
- Optional: delivery constraints the human states (ordering preferences, what must ship first).

## Files to read

- `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/change.md` — problem, outcome, operations, acceptance,
  out of scope, and open questions.
- `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/proposed/**` — every proposed future-state artifact; the
  overlay these slices implement.
- Baseline artifacts under `docs/product/model` referenced by the change's operations or by the
  proposed artifacts' relationships.
- `templates/delivery-slice.yaml` — the slice template and field comments.
- `docs/specification/delivery-slices.md` — the normative slice contract.
- `skills/slice-product-change/references/slicing-heuristics.md` — vertical-outcome heuristics
  and anti-patterns.

## Deterministic commands

- `prodshape inspect <ID>` — relationships of any artifact you are grouping into a slice.
- `prodshape impact <ID> --direction both` — what an artifact's inclusion drags along.
- `prodshape change validate <CHG-ID>` — validates the overlay and the slice files:
  references resolve (PRODUCT006), slices name their containing change (PRODUCT030), partial
  coverage has a scope (PRODUCT031), dependencies do not cycle (PRODUCT032).
- `prodshape validate --change <CHG-ID> --format json` — machine-readable diagnostics.

## Reasoning procedure

1. Confirm the change status is `approved` by reading `change.md`. If it is not, stop and report;
   do not slice an unapproved change.
2. Read the whole change: `change.md` and every file under `proposed/`. Build a picture of what
   the product can do after the change that it cannot do now.
3. Identify vertical product outcomes: statements of the form "an actor can do X end to end".
   Each candidate slice must have exactly one such `outcome` sentence, phrased in product terms.
   If a candidate's outcome can only be phrased in system terms ("the persistence layer supports
   handoffs"), it is not a slice — regroup until it is.
4. Reject technical-layer slicing explicitly. No "backend slice", "frontend slice", "database
   slice", no slice-per-endpoint, no slice-per-screen. Apply
   `references/slicing-heuristics.md` to every candidate cut line.
5. Map requirements to slices. For each slice, list which Functional Requirements, Quality
   Requirements and Constraints of the change's overlay it implements. Coverage is `full` only
   when the requirement is done when the slice is done; otherwise declare `partial` with a
   precise `scope` sentence naming exactly which part this slice covers and, where useful, which
   slice covers the rest. Honest partial coverage beats optimistic full coverage.
6. Identify dependencies. `depends-on` lists slices of the same change whose product outcome this
   slice genuinely builds on — not a technical build order. Prefer independent slices; verify no
   cycles by inspection before validation catches them.
7. Declare `affects` (artifacts touched beyond the implemented requirements), `verification`
   (non-empty, in product terms: what can be observed or exercised when the slice works) and
   `out-of-scope` (explicit exclusions, so nobody infers a promise the slice never made).
8. Write one YAML file per slice under `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/slices/`, from
   `templates/delivery-slice.yaml`: `id: SLI-<AREA>-<NNN>`, `status: draft` (or `proposed` when
   the human asks the slicing to be put forward), `product-change: <CHG-ID>`.
9. Run `prodshape change validate <CHG-ID>`. Fix every error, re-run until clean.
   Report warnings — notably PRODUCT109 (slice affecting artifacts outside its requirements'
   closure) — and either justify or correct them.
10. Present the slicing rationale to the human: each slice's outcome, why the cut lines fall
    where they do, the coverage table (which requirement, which slice, full or partial-with-scope,
    confirming every requirement the change introduces or modifies is accounted for), the
    dependency order, and any coverage gaps left deliberately open.

## Allowed modifications

- Create and edit YAML files under `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/slices/`.
- Append newly discovered product questions to the change's `## Open Questions` section.

## Forbidden actions

- Never set any slice status to `approved`, `in-progress` or `completed` — approval is human-only.
- Never modify `docs/product/model`, the change's operations, or its `proposed/` artifacts to
  make slicing easier; if the change itself needs revision, report it instead.
- Never run `prodshape change promote`.
- Never slice by technical layer, endpoint or screen.
- Never declare `partial` coverage without a precise `scope`, and never declare `full` coverage
  you cannot defend.
- Never create backlog items or handoffs; those follow slice approval.
- Never invent product decisions to close a coverage gap; record the question instead.
- Never substitute your own judgment for `prodshape change validate` output.

## Human approval points

- Each slice's move to `approved` is a human decision (approval point 2 of the Change operation).
  Present the proposal; do not approve.
- Whether a slice is a _good_ increment — coherent, valuable, honestly scoped — is a judgment no
  tool makes and this skill only argues for; the human decides.
- Any change to the Product Change itself that slicing reveals as necessary goes back to the
  human before it is made.

## Expected outputs

- One `sli-*.yaml` per slice under `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/slices/`, each with
  outcome, implements (with coverage and scopes), affects, depends-on, verification and
  out-of-scope filled, status `draft` or `proposed`.
- A written slicing rationale: outcomes, cut-line reasoning, coverage table, dependency order,
  and open points for the approver.

## Completion checks

- `prodshape change validate <CHG-ID>` exits 0 with no errors; warnings are reported
  with a justification or a fix.
- Every slice's `outcome` names something an actor can do, not a system property.
- Every requirement added or modified by the change appears in at least one slice's `implements`,
  or its absence is called out explicitly in the rationale.
- Every `partial` coverage entry carries a precise `scope`; no slice status exceeds `proposed`.
- No slice is a technical layer, endpoint or screen; `depends-on` contains no cycles.
